items.meaning: A shop places the next-day order from a phone or the shop PC until 16:00.
items.row: Every shop can place the next-day order from a phone or the shop PC, until 16:00. MUST

items.meaning: The order form shows the previous order so it can be copied and adjusted.
items.row: The order form shows yesterday's order so you can copy it and change the numbers. (Important!!)

items.meaning: Products out of production that day are shown greyed out, not hidden.
items.row: Products that are out of production for the day are greyed out, not hidden.

items.meaning: The central bakery sees all orders in one list by 16:15 and can print it per oven line.
items.row: Central bakery sees all orders in one list by 16:15 and can print it per oven line.

items.meaning: A shop manager can set a standing order per weekday, created automatically unless changed by 15:30.
items.row: a shop manager can set a standing order per weekday that is created automatically if nobody changes it by 15:30 ***

items.meaning: Order confirmation with totals goes to the shop by SMS and email.
items.row: Order confirmation goes to the shop by SMS and email (or whatsapp?) with the totals.

items.meaning: At closing the shop records what was thrown away per product and a report compares it with the order.
items.row: Wastage: at closing the shop types what was thrown away per product; the report compares with the order. nice to have

items.meaning: The order form also shows the same weekday of the previous week.
items.row: Same as 2 basically: show last week same day as well, Dana asked for this twice.

items.meaning: The allergen list per product is visible in the order form.
items.row: Allergen list per product visible in the order form (legal, must).

items.meaning: Prices are set centrally; shops cannot edit them.
items.row: Price changes are set centrally and shops cannot edit prices.

items.meaning: If the bakery cannot deliver the full quantity, the shop is told before 06:00 what is short.
items.row: If the bakery cannot deliver the full quantity, the shop is told before 06:00 what is short.

items.meaning: The driver scans the crate label at drop-off so the shop knows the order arrived.
items.row: Driver app: scan the crate label at drop-off so the shop knows the order arrived. (phase 2?)

items.meaning: Unsold bread returned to the central bakery for the animal feed partner is counted per crate.
items.row: Returns of unsold bread to the central bakery for the animal feed partner, counted per crate.

items.meaning: Owners see sales, orders and wastage per shop per week on a dashboard.
items.row: the dashboard for the owners: sales vs orders vs wastage per shop per week. must

items.meaning: Roles: shop manager, shop staff (order only), bakery planner, driver, owner.
items.row: Users: shop manager, shop staff (order only, no standing orders), bakery planner, driver, owner.

items.meaning: The shop can keep ordering offline and it syncs when the connection returns.
items.row: Works offline in the shop if the internet drops, syncs later. should

items.meaning: The order cut-off time can differ per shop.
items.row: Order cut-off time can be different per shop (the airport shop closes late).

items.meaning: A shortage notice names the replacement product when there is one.
items.row: See 11 - also tell them the replacement product if there is one.

must_not_invent: WhatsApp confirmation as a requirement (it is a question in the source)
notes: Item 6 is ambiguous: WhatsApp is a question, not a channel. Item 12 says "phase 2?", so it stays an item, flagged ambiguous for scope. Item 8 restates 2 with a second window (last week): it stays a row, and a duplicate flag pointing at G01-02 is expected, with "last week" kept in its reader version. The meeting notes and the parking line are not rows.
